name.text: Calculating theoretical probability for a token drawing experiment

questiontext.text:
A mathematics teacher in Kisumu prepares a cloth bag containing coloured plastic tokens for a probability experiment. The bag contains {@num_red@} red tokens and {@num_blue@} blue tokens.

[[jsxgraph width="420px" height="300px"]] (function() { var n1 = {#num_red#}, n2 = {#num_blue#}, per = 6; var rows = Math.ceil(n1/per) + Math.ceil(n2/per); var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox:[-1, rows + 2.6, 10.5, -1.2], axis:false, grid:false, keepaspectratio:true, showNavigation:false, showCopyright:false, pan:{enabled:false}, zoom:{enabled:false}}); b.create('polygon', [[-0.4,-0.4],[per+0.4,-0.4],[per+0.4,rows+0.2],[-0.4,rows+0.2]], {fillColor:'#efebe9', fillOpacity:0.7, vertices:{visible:false}, borders:{strokeColor:'#8d6e63', strokeWidth:2}, fixed:true}); var row = rows - 0.5, col = 0; function put(n, colr) { for (var i = 0; i < n; i++) { b.create('point', [col + 0.5, row], {name:'', size:9, fixed:true, fillColor:colr, strokeColor:'#333', showInfobox:false}); col++; if (col === per) { col = 0; row -= 1; } } if (col !== 0) { col = 0; row -= 1; } } put(n1, '#e53935'); put(n2, '#1e88e5'); b.create('point', [7.2, rows - 0.3], {name:'', size:7, fixed:true, fillColor:'#e53935', strokeColor:'#333', showInfobox:false}); b.create('text', [7.6, rows - 0.3, 'red (' + n1 + ')'], {fontSize:13, fixed:true, anchorY:'middle'}); b.create('point', [7.2, rows - 1.3], {name:'', size:7, fixed:true, fillColor:'#1e88e5', strokeColor:'#333', showInfobox:false}); b.create('text', [7.6, rows - 1.3, 'blue (' + n2 + ')'], {fontSize:13, fixed:true, anchorY:'middle'}); b.create('text', [per/2, rows + 1.3, 'Bag of tokens'], {fontSize:14, fixed:true, anchorX:'middle'}); })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

A student is asked to close their eyes and draw exactly {@draw_total@} tokens simultaneously from the bag.

a) Calculate the total number of possible combinations for drawing {@draw_total@} tokens from the entire bag.

\(n(S) =\) [[input:ans1]]

[[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

b) Calculate the number of possible outcomes where the student draws exactly {@req_red@} red token(s) and {@req_blue@} blue token(s).

\(n(E) =\) [[input:ans2]]

[[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

c) Using your results from parts (a) and (b), determine the theoretical probability of this exact combination occurring.

(Enter your answer as a fraction).

\(P(\text{exact combination}) =\) [[input:ans3]]

[[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt3]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

Part a: The Sample Space
The bag contains a total of \({@num_red@} + {@num_blue@} = {@total_tokens@}\) tokens. We are drawing a subset of \({@draw_total@}\) tokens. Using the combinations formula:

\( \displaystyle n(S) = {}^{{@total_tokens@}}C_{{@draw_total@}} = \frac{{@total_tokens@}!}{{@draw_total@}!({@total_tokens@} - {@draw_total@})!} = {@ta1@} \)

Part b: The Favourable Outcomes
The event requires choosing exactly \({@req_red@}\) token(s) from the \({@num_red@}\) red tokens, AND \({@req_blue@}\) token(s) from the \({@num_blue@}\) blue tokens. Because these are drawn from two distinct groups, we multiply their independent combinations:

\( \displaystyle n(E) = {}^{{@num_red@}}C_{{@req_red@}} \times {}^{{@num_blue@}}C_{{@req_blue@}} \)

\( \displaystyle n(E) = {@red_comb@} \times {@blue_comb@} = {@ta2@} \)

Part c: The Theoretical Probability
Theoretical probability is defined as the number of favourable outcomes divided by the total number of equally-likely outcomes in the sample space:

\( \displaystyle P(E) = \frac{n(E)}{n(S)} = \frac{{@ta2@}}{{@ta1@}} \)

Simplifying this fraction mathematically gives the final probability:

\( \displaystyle \boxed{ {@ta3@} } \)

questionnote.text: Red: {@num_red@}, Blue: {@num_blue@}. Draw: {@draw_total@}. Req R: {@req_red@}, Req B: {@req_blue@}. n(S)={@ta1@}, n(E)={@ta2@}, P={@ta3@}

questiondescription.text:
This question is based on Example 1 (drawing marbles of two colours, counting with combinations) in the section Theoretical Probability of the CBC Grade 11 Mathematics textbook (INNODEMS).

Theoretical Probability (Combinations)

node.description: Check absolute correctness of sample space

truefeedback.text: Correct. You successfully calculated the combinations for the entire sample space.

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. To find the total sample space \(n(S)\), use the combinations formula \({}^nC_r\) where \(n\) is the TOTAL number of tokens in the bag, and \(r\) is the number being drawn.

node.description: Check absolute correctness of favourable outcomes

truefeedback.text: Correct. You successfully identified the number of favourable combination selections.

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. Remember to calculate the combinations for the red tokens and the combinations for the blue tokens separately, then multiply them together to find \(n(E)\).

node.description: Algebraic equivalence of final probability fraction
Check if they simply divided their own potentially wrong n(E) by n(S)

truefeedback.text: You correctly applied the formula \(P(E) = \frac{n(E)}{n(S)}\) based on your previous answers, but because one of your earlier calculations was incorrect, your final probability is also incorrect.

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. Theoretical probability is found by dividing the number of favourable outcomes \(n(E)\) by the total outcomes in the sample space \(n(S)\).
